## Bertrand Russell quote sources

9 passages attributed to Bertrand Russell in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Russell.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Bertrand Russell

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

### Sourcing profile

Language of the works

English

Cited here from

The Conquest of Happiness, A Free Man's Worship, Why I Am Not a Christian, the Autobiography, and A History of Western Philosophy.

How to cite it

Original essay title and year, not the title of the collection you happen to own. Russell's essays were gathered into several different volumes, in Britain and America, under different titles.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

The same essay circulates under two or three titles, so two readers can appear to be citing different works when they are citing one. His shorter pieces were also written for magazines and lectures, which means the polished standalone aphorism is often a passage from an occasional piece rather than a sustained statement of position.

1 of the passages below have been worked through against the cited edition, with the original-language wording and the circulating variants recorded on their own pages.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Where can I check quotations attributed to Bertrand Russell?

Original essay title and year, not the title of the collection you happen to own. Russell's essays were gathered into several different volumes, in Britain and America, under different titles. This archive cites Bertrand Russell from The Conquest of Happiness, A Free Man's Worship, Why I Am Not a Christian, the Autobiography, and A History of Western Philosophy. Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

#### What is the most common mistake when quoting Bertrand Russell?

The same essay circulates under two or three titles, so two readers can appear to be citing different works when they are citing one. His shorter pieces were also written for magazines and lectures, which means the polished standalone aphorism is often a passage from an occasional piece rather than a sustained statement of position.

#### What language did Bertrand Russell write in?

English. For an author writing in English the wording is settled at source, but editions and titles are not — see the citation note above.
